result.title: When the Critic Falls Behind: Co-Evolving Rubrics and Harnesses for Continual Agent Self-Improvement
result.summary: Autonomous agents increasingly depend on harnesses that govern interaction, memory, tools, and execution around large language models (LLMs). While recent work has begun to evolve these harnesses from execution experience, the supervision used to guide evolution often remains relatively static, making it difficult to track changing behavioral weaknesses across rounds and potentially limiting generalization to unseen tasks. To address this issue, we propose RuHarness, a rubric--harness co-evolution framework for continual agent self-improvement. RuHarness continually discovers and reassesses behavioral criteria from execution trajectories, prioritizes the most relevant unresolved weaknesses, and uses them to guide targeted harness updates while keeping the task objective fixed. Extensive experiments across diverse agent tasks and backbone models show that RuHarness outperforms strong harness-evolution baselines, particularly on unseen held-out tasks. Further analyses show that adaptive rubric prioritization tracks shifting weaknesses and supports more sustained improvement and stable generalization across evolution rounds.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 RuHarness，从执行轨迹中持续发现并重估行为准则（rubrics），优先针对尚未解决的弱点定向更新 agent harness，从而在多轮演化中实现持续的自我改进。
AI.relevance_reason: 研究对象是纯文本 agent 的交互、记忆与工具框架，并非 VLM 视觉推理，但其从轨迹自动生成并按相关性排序监督准则的做法，可能为 latent 推理轨迹中的弱点定位与监督/贡献分配提供可供核查的线索。
